subject: Post-call: spend range sensitivity and PO pathway
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Sinclair <avery.sinclair@brightline.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-03T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: spend range sensitivity and PO pathway

Hi Avery — thanks again for the 30-min demo earlier. Quick recap and the asks I promised: 

1) What we heard you using today and where Redwood would sit
- Inference patterns: real-time chat for agents (~70% of tokens) + nightly batch embeddings for recommendations (~30%).
- Peak concurrency is light (60–90 RPS) but monthly volume is the main cost driver.

2) Quick qualification (needs from you)
- Target monthly spend band: approximately which of the bands below feels closest to Brightline?
  • $10k–$25k/mo
  • $25k–$75k/mo
  • $75k–$200k/mo
  • $200k+/mo
- Procurement requirements: PO threshold, payment terms (Net30/Net45/Net60), any legal must-haves we should surface up front.
- Target $/1M tokens you’d consider comfortable for a committed offer (ballpark is fine).

3) Pricing/commit options I suggested on the call (examples, not final):
- Option A: No commit / pay-as-you-go (higher unit $). Good for pilots.
- Option B: 6-month pilot commit — blended price target ~$X / 1M tokens, refundable credits for usage overage; requires PO >= $40k.
- Option C: 12-month reserved band — improved unit economics (~lowest $/1M) and SLA; typically requires a purchase order and finance approval.

4) Next steps I propose (pick one):
- You confirm the monthly band + PO threshold — I’ll prepare a tailored 6-month pilot deck and a draft SOW.
- Or we run a 2-week low-cost spike pilot to measure real token velocity and produce exact cost examples.

I’ll attach a short CSV with illustrative cost calc (samples across quantization + batching) and a draft proposal for the bands — just to make the trade-offs concrete.

Thanks — cc’ing Karthik for pricing/commit details.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: cost_examples.csv (sample cost calc), redwood-proposal-draft.pdf (banded options)
From: Avery Sinclair <avery.sinclair@brightline.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-03T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: spend range sensitivity and PO pathway

Jordan — thanks for the recap, that aligns well. A few quick data points from our side: 

- Likely monthly band: $50k–$100k/mo to start (we expect growth if pilot shows saver latency/cost).
- Procurement: PO required for committed work; finance typically needs PO >= $50k to avoid special approvals.
- Payment terms: Net60 is our standard for new vendors.
- Target $/1M tokens: we’d be comfortable evaluating offers around $350–$600 per 1M tokens depending on latency guarantees and KV cache behavior.

Questions: 
- Can Redwood do a fixed unit on a 6-month pilot that caps at $600/1M tokens with an escalator if usage exceeds X tokens?
- How quickly do you expect to provide measured token velocity after the spike pilot? We need numbers for our internal forecast in ~2 weeks.

If you can send concrete examples tied to our band I’ll route to procurement — cc’ing our procurement lead separately if needed.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Sinclair
Head of Platform, Brightline
avery.sinclair@brightline.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Sinclair <avery.sinclair@brightline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-04T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: spend range sensitivity and PO pathway

Avery — great, appreciate the clarity. Short answers and attached examples: 

- Yes, we can structure a 6-month pilot that floors at $600/1M tokens for the first X tokens, with a step-down to $450/1M after a committed volume threshold is met (illustrative only). The attached cost_examples.csv models three scenarios:
  • conservative (no quantization, conservative batching) = ~$620/1M
  • optimized (dynamic batching + 8-bit quant) = ~$380/1M
  • reserved pool (dedicated instances + caching) = ~$300/1M

- Measured token velocity: if we run a 2-week spike pilot (instrumented) we can give you a token usage report within 5 business days after the spike ends — enough for your forecasting.

Procurement Path: to keep things moving, recommended lane:
- If PO >= $50k and Net60 is acceptable, we can sign a 6-month SOW that describes the pilot, deliverables, and billing cadence. Legal asks we typically see are limited — we can provision an SOC2 attestation and standard DP addendum.

I’m looping Karthik for a quick confirmation on pricing guardrails and to draft the SOW with PO-friendly billing.

Onboarding plan (if you pick the pilot):
1) Sign SOW/PO (procurement)
2) Kickoff + integration (1 week)
3) 2-week spike pilot (collect telemetry)
4) 5 business day token velocity report -> finalize commit band and price step-downs

Let me know if that timeline works and whether procurement needs a formal quote PDF to start routing.

—Jordan

Attachments: cost_examples.csv, redwood-proposal-draft.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-04T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: recommended PO lane and pricing guardrails for Brightline

Jordan / Marissa — quick internal note after reviewing Avery’s constraints and the attached cost examples. Recommended approach: 

1) Procurement lane (fastest to close): 6-month pilot SOW, PO billing monthly, Net60 terms. Require minimum PO >= $50k to avoid extra finance approvals.

2) Pricing guardrails (proposal language) — keep ranges in the SOW: 
- Pilot floor: $600 / 1M tokens up to 500M tokens total in the pilot window.
- Step-down: $450 / 1M once cumulative tokens exceed 500M within the 6-month period.
- Overage: PAYG at $700 / 1M above agreed caps.

3) Commercially sensible defaults: include SOC2 attestation link, standard DP addendum, and a 30-day SLA credit clause for sustained availability regressions.

4) Next actions: Jordan to send a one-page quote PDF to Brightline to enable routing to procurement. Marissa, can you pull the standard 6-month SOW template and confirm billing language (monthly invoices with PO ref)? I’ll prepare the pricing clauses and attach to the draft.

If we get a PO within 10 business days we can begin kickoff in week 2.

—Karthik
Finance & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
